one_liner: Auto-tuned OpenCL BLAS (levels 1-3, FP16, batched) for GPUs and accelerators; beats clBLAS GEMM, trails cuBLAS on NVIDIA.
what_it_does: A C++11 BLAS library whose kernels are OpenCL C, covering almost all Netlib BLAS routines in S/D/C/Z and half precision, plus non-standard batched, strided-batched, im2col and convolution-as-GEMM routines. The main API (clblast.h, or clblast_c.h for C) is modelled on clBLAS: callers pass cl_mem device buffers plus a cl_command_queue and manage host-device transfers themselves, with no library initialisation call. An optional Netlib CBLAS layer (cblas_sgemm etc., CMake -DNETLIB=ON) copies host buffers to the default device automatically, and a beta CUDA/NVRTC build (-DCUDA=ON -DOPENCL=OFF) replaces the OpenCL API.
how_it_is_fast: Every kernel is parameterised (the GEMM kernel has 14 parameters: work-group tile sizes MWG/NWG, 2D register tiling MWI/NWI, vector widths VWM/VWN, unroll factor KWI, local-memory use) and auto-tuned per device in the style of CLTune, with a shipped database of best values for many NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Arm Mali, Qualcomm Adreno and Apple GPUs. GEMM has two paths: an indirect path that pads/transposes inputs with pre- and post-processing kernels so a fast main kernel can assume tile-multiple sizes, and a single 'direct' kernel for small matrices; a routine-level tuner picks the size at which to switch. FP16 routines and batched GEMM give further gains on hardware with fast half precision or many small problems.
when_to_use: You need GEMM or other BLAS on non-NVIDIA GPUs (AMD, Intel integrated or Arc, Arm Mali, Qualcomm Adreno, Apple M-series) through OpenCL, and clBLAS is the alternative.
Irregular or rectangular matrix sizes where clBLAS loses badly; you can tune for your exact shapes with the tuners or the tuning API and OverrideParameters.
Mobile and embedded GPUs where half precision (cl_khr_fp16) is accelerated, e.g. deep-learning inference on Mali or Intel GPUs.
Many small matrices at once: GEMMBATCHED or the faster GEMMSTRIDEDBATCHED instead of a loop of single GEMM calls.
Portable code that must run across vendors, or OpenCL 1.1-era hardware.
when_not_to_use: NVIDIA-only deployments: the README itself says to use cuBLAS there, and the IWOCL '18 paper shows cuBLAS still faster.
CPU BLAS work (it is not a replacement for OpenBLAS, MKL, BLIS or Eigen); Intel CPUs are only reachable through an OpenCL CPU runtime.
You need LAPACK (factorisations, solvers, eigenvalues): only BLAS is implemented, and xROTG, xROTMG, xROT, xROTM, xTBSV and xTPSV are missing.
Untuned devices where you cannot run the tuners: the README warns out-of-the-box performance can be poor and falls back to family defaults.

Correctness-critical work on devices with open accuracy reports (e.g. CGEMM errors on AMD RX 5700 in issue #669, SSYRK/SSYR2K error on Apple M1 in #668, FP16 GEMV in #561) unless you run the bundled correctness tests on your device first.

integration.form: shared lib (static via -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF); packages in Debian/Ubuntu (libclblast-dev), Homebrew, Windows release zips; Python binding pyclblast
integration.dependencies: OpenCL 1.1+ runtime and headers (or CUDA 7.5+ with NVRTC for the CUDA build); nothing else
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (GCC 4.7+, Clang 3.3+, MSVC 2013+ per docs); CMakeLists now requires CMake 3.14 although installation.md still says 2.8.10
integration.platforms: Any OpenCL 1.1+ device: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPUs and CPUs, Arm Mali, Qualcomm Adreno, Apple M1/M2, Intel MIC; Linux, macOS, Windows, Android (cross-compile)
integration.thread_safety: Library made thread-safe in 0.7.0; a multithreading bug in the compiled-kernel cache was fixed in 1.6.1, so use 1.6.1 or newer for multithreaded callers
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the main API mirrors clBLAS argument order (cl_mem buffers, offsets, queue, event) so porting from clBLAS is mostly renaming; not link-compatible with clBLAS, and the CBLAS-named Netlib layer works but copies host data each call and is documented as not for full performance control

gotchas: First call of each routine compiles its OpenCL kernel at run time, so first-call latency is high; use FillCache(device) to precompile, and ClearCache to free the binaries.

Indirect GEMM may allocate a temporary device buffer (error -4 on memory-tight devices); query GemmTempBufferSize and pass your own buffer, or raise the direct/indirect switch point with OverrideParameters.
Versions 1.6.2 and older give wrong results on Intel Arc A770 and some other devices (GEMMK=1 kernel bug when MWG!=NWG, fixed in 1.6.3); distro packages may ship an older version.

GemmStridedBatched with a C stride of 0 does not accumulate into one matrix (open issue #578); FP16 tests can fail on operation order, and integer-returning half routines (IHAMAX etc.) are not properly tested.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only GPU/OpenCL library among the catalogued blas-lapack siblings: pick it when the matrices live on a GPU or mobile accelerator; pick BLASFEO, LibShalom or Eigen for small or medium matrices on CPUs, and FT-BLAS or GEMMFIP when you need a CPU BLAS replacement for OpenBLAS/MKL.
verified_claims_summary: The peer-reviewed IWOCL '18 paper benchmarks CLBlast 1.3.0 GEMM against clBLAS 2.12 (and cuBLAS on NVIDIA) on seven devices (GTX 750 Ti, Titan X, Radeon HD 7970, Radeon M370X, Intel Skylake GT2, Core i5-6200U CPU, Mali T628) and reports better overall GEMM throughput than clBLAS, most visibly at irregular sizes (multiples of 129) and on Skylake and NVIDIA, shown in graphs without a numeric ratio; cuBLAS remained faster. The ~2x FP16 and up-to-10x batched figures compare CLBlast with its own FP32 and non-batched calls, not with another library.
status_note: Actively maintained (1.7.0 is the latest release, commits into September 2026, tuning results still being added), Apache-2.0 and packaged by major distros, so it is usable as-is; plan to run the tuners and correctness tests on devices outside its tuned list.
